ordered_diagnoses: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries

facts.raw_span: Initial serum troponin I level: 0.070 ng/mL
Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
Negative P waves in lead I
Initial serum troponin I level: 0.070 ng/mL
Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery
Right atrium and right ventricle lay on the left side, left atrium and left ventricle lay on the right side
ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6
Negative P waves in lead I

concepts.why: The patient presented with chest pain, elevated serum troponin I level, and total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, which are all indicative of a heart attack.
The patient's right atrium and right ventricle are located on the left side, and the left atrium and left ventricle are located on the right side, which is a characteristic of dextrocardia.
The patient has a total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, which is a sign of coronary artery disease.
The patient's internal organs are reversed or mirrored from their normal positions, which is a characteristic of sitrus inversus.
The patient has ST-segment elevations in leads I, II, III, aVF, and V4 through V6, and a total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery, which are indicative of a right ventricular infarction.

rationales.F09: Total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery is a strong indicator of acute myocardial infarction and coronary artery disease.
rationales.F10: The abnormal position of the heart chambers is consistent with dextrocardia, situs inversus, and congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries.
rationales.F11: ST-segment elevations are a strong indicator of acute myocardial infarction and coronary artery disease.
rationales.F12: Negative P waves in lead I are consistent with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries.
